findings.issue_text: P2: Backup code single-use consumption is not atomic — read-decrypt, indexOf, write, re-encrypt, update flow allows concurrent logins to both pass the check and last-writer-wins resurrects a consumed code; needs atomic/conditional update or serialization

P2: Unhandled JSON.parse on decrypted backup codes (next-auth-options.ts ~line 143 and disable.ts ~line 55) turns corrupt/non-JSON stored data into a 500 during login or disable; non-array valid JSON also breaks indexOf behavior

P2: Escape/overlay-close on the DisplayBackupCodes step in EnableTwoFactorModal skips resetState()/onEnable(), leaving parent uninformed, step stuck on backup-codes view, and stale backupCodes/backupCodesUrl never cleared by resetState

P2: /two-factor/totp/setup endpoint overwrites existing backupCodes (and secret) before setup is confirmed, destroying previously valid recovery codes if the user re-enters or abandons setup; should persist codes only on successful enable

P3: Non-string backupCode body value (array/number/object) makes .replaceAll throw an unhandled TypeError (500) instead of returning IncorrectBackupCode in disable.ts and next-auth-options.ts; should guard with typeof check
P3: Exhausted backup codes (array of nulls) return IncorrectBackupCode instead of MissingBackupCodes, giving users a misleading message when all codes have been used
P3: Login page backupCode field may be stripped by zodResolver if not added to formSchema, silently breaking backup-code login; need confirmation schema was updated
Note: disable-via-backup-code sets backupCodes to null (deleting all codes) rather than consuming a single code — flagged to confirm this asymmetry with the login flow is intentional
P1: Backup code verification is a non-atomic read-modify-write, allowing a single-use code to be consumed twice via concurrent sign-in requests (next-auth-options.ts ~145-155)
P2: Backup code comparison uses indexOf instead of a constant-time comparison like crypto.timingSafeEqual (next-auth-options.ts ~150, disable.ts ~58)
P2: disable.ts two-factor endpoint has no per-attempt throttling beyond global rate limiting

P2: Unhandled JSON.parse on decrypted backup codes with no validation that the result is an array of strings, causing 500s on disable and generic sign-in failures, potentially persisting garbage via write-back, and permanently locking users out of backup-code recovery (disable.ts ~56, next-auth-options.ts ~143)
P2: req.body.backupCode.replaceAll called without type checking, causing unhandled 500 crash when backupCode is not a string (disable.ts ~58)
P2: Setup endpoint overwrites user.backupCodes before 2FA is enabled, silently destroying a user's existing valid recovery codes if setup is abandoned (setup.ts ~60-66)
P3: No UI or endpoint to re-display backup codes; users who close the modal without saving are locked into TOTP-only with codes never recorded (EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx)
setup.ts lacks the encryption key null-check that disable.ts has, though it follows the file's pre-existing pattern
Object URL leak in EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx (~line 92-99): createObjectURL result is never revoked on component unmount, leaking a Blob per modal open/setup/close cycle

Backup-code 'mark used' operation in next-auth-options.ts (~line 140-150) rewrites and re-encrypts the entire JSON array on every backup-code login instead of a targeted update (per-login write amplification)
setup.ts regenerates/overwrites backup codes on every setup call even if 2FA setup is later abandoned (correctness/security concern)
Null-sentinel JSON array for backup codes in next-auth-options.ts will serialize null entries (correctness/security concern)

backupCode likely stripped by zod schema before reaching NextAuth credentials provider: formSchema not updated in diff, so zodResolver drops backupCode from submit payload, silently breaking backup-code login
Unvalidated req.body.backupCode type can throw TypeError in totp/disable endpoint, returning unhandled 500 instead of documented 400 ErrorCode.IncorrectBackupCode response

Setup endpoint response adds backupCodes field but client (EnableTwoFactorModal) calls body.backupCodes.map with no existence check, crashing on stale API/older backend and leaving 2FA in half-configured state

Disable endpoint consumes backup codes differently from login flow (code validated but not burned individually), creating a latent contract asymmetry if an early return is added between validation and final update

P1: Backup code single-use enforcement has a race condition — non-atomic read-modify-write (decrypt → indexOf → prisma.user.update of whole array) allows a backup code to be used twice under concurrent login requests; no transaction, conditional UPDATE, or row lock in packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts:148-155

P2: Unguarded JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...)) — corrupt stored backupCodes throws an unhandled exception, returning a 500 in the API route and a generic auth failure in authorize, leaving the user with no path to disable or recover 2FA (apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts:56, packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts:139-141)

P2: ErrorCode.InternalServerError is thrown rather than returned in the disable endpoint, producing a raw 500 HTML page instead of the JSON { error } shape clients expect to parse via response.json() (apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts:47)

P2: Unvalidated backupCode body type — req.body.backupCode used directly; a non-string (number, object) makes replaceAll throw, causing an unhandled 500; credentials.backupCode in next-auth-options.ts is similarly not runtime-validated

P2: Backup codes persisted at setup time before 2FA is enabled and never regenerated — abandoned setup leaves stored codes, closing the DisplayBackupCodes step without copying loses the codes permanently, and there is no regenerate path short of disabling and re-enabling 2FA (apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/setup.ts:60-65)

P3: navigator.clipboard used without availability guard in EnableTwoFactorModal copy handler — undefined in non-secure contexts (plain HTTP, some webviews), so the click throws silently with no feedback or fallback

P3: Backup code matching is case-sensitive — codes are lowercase hex but compared verbatim, so uppercase input is rejected as incorrect; should normalize with .toLowerCase() on both sides (next-auth-options.ts:145, disable.ts:58)
P3: Object URL never revoked on dialog close/unmount in EnableTwoFactorModal — backupCodesUrl is revoked only when replaced, so blob leaks accumulate per setup attempt

Unchecked JSON.parse on decrypted stored backup codes will throw on malformed/legacy values, causing an unhandled 500 in disable.ts or opaque auth failure in next-auth; should be wrapped in try/catch surfacing MissingBackupCodes/InternalServerError

Dialog onOpenChange (backdrop/ESC close) in EnableTwoFactorModal doesn't call resetState(), so reopening after closing at DisplayBackupCodes re-displays old backup codes instead of starting at ConfirmPassword
Backup-code comparison uses non-constant-time indexOf string equality; should use crypto.timingSafeEqual for security-sensitive credential verification
Component in BackupCode.tsx is named TwoFactor, mismatching the file and import name BackupCode, a maintenance trap conflating it with the real TwoFactor component
Backup-code XXXXX-XXXXX format logic is implicitly duplicated across formatBackupCode, BackupCode placeholder, and two dash-strip call sites with no shared constant
New i18n keys (backup_code, lost_access, etc.) added only to the en locale; other locales will render raw keys or fall back

goldens.comment: The exported function TwoFactor handles backup codes and is in BackupCode.tsx. Inconsistent naming.
Error message mentions 'backup code login' but this is a disable endpoint, not login

Backup code validation is case-sensitive due to the use of indexOf(). This causes validation to fail if a user enters uppercase hex characters, as backup codes should be case-insensitive for a better user experience.

Because backupCodes are decrypted and mutated in memory before being written back, two concurrent login requests using the same backupCode could both pass this check and update, so a single backup code may effectively be accepted more than once if used concurrently, weakening the intended one-time-use semantics.

Object URL for backup codes is not revoked on component unmount, leading to a potential memory leak. This can cause increased memory usage over time, especially if the component is mounted and unmounted frequently.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: Backup code single-use consumption is not atomic — read-decrypt, indexOf, write, re-encrypt, update flow allows concurrent logins to both pass the check and last-writer-wins resurrects a consumed code; needs atomic/conditional update or serialization

P2: Unhandled JSON.parse on decrypted backup codes (next-auth-options.ts ~line 143 and disable.ts ~line 55) turns corrupt/non-JSON stored data into a 500 during login or disable; non-array valid JSON also breaks indexOf behavior

adjudication.rationale: In both `packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts` (backup-code branch in `authorize`) and `apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts` (backup code path), the code does `JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...))` with no try/catch or shape validation. If `user.backupCodes` decrypts to corrupt/non-JSON (or even valid non-array JSON like an object), `JSON.parse` or subsequent `backupCodes.indexOf(...)` can throw (e.g., `indexOf is not a function`), causing a 500 during login or 2FA disable rather than returning a controlled error response.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: Escape/overlay-close on the DisplayBackupCodes step in EnableTwoFactorModal skips resetState()/onEnable(), leaving parent uninformed, step stuck on backup-codes view, and stale backupCodes/backupCodesUrl never cleared by resetState

adjudication.rationale: In EnableTwoFactorModal, successful enable now does `setStep(SetupStep.DisplayBackupCodes)` and defers `onEnable()` until the explicit “close” button in the DisplayBackupCodes step. However, the Dialog is controlled via `open`/`onOpenChange={onOpenChange}` with no wrapper to call `resetState()` or `onEnable()` when the dialog is dismissed via overlay click/ESC. That means the modal can close without notifying the parent (`onEnable` not called) and without resetting local state, so reopening can show the stale `step === DisplayBackupCodes` and previously generated `backupCodes`/`backupCodesUrl`. Additionally, `resetState()` does not clear `backupCodes` or revoke/clear `backupCodesUrl`, so even paths that call resetState keep stale backup-code state around.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: /two-factor/totp/setup endpoint overwrites existing backupCodes (and secret) before setup is confirmed, destroying previously valid recovery codes if the user re-enters or abandons setup; should persist codes only on successful enable

adjudication.rationale: In `apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/setup.ts`, the setup endpoint immediately generates and persists a new `backupCodes` set and a new `twoFactorSecret` via `prisma.user.update({ data: { backupCodes: ..., twoFactorEnabled: false, twoFactorSecret: ... }})` before the user completes the enable confirmation step. This necessarily overwrites any previously stored `backupCodes` (and the secret) on every setup call, so re-running or abandoning setup can destroy previously valid recovery codes/secret state.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P3: Non-string backupCode body value (array/number/object) makes .replaceAll throw an unhandled TypeError (500) instead of returning IncorrectBackupCode in disable.ts and next-auth-options.ts; should guard with typeof check

adjudication.rationale: In both new backup-code flows, the code assumes the provided backup code is a string and calls `.replaceAll` directly. In `apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts`, it does `req.body.backupCode.replaceAll("-", "")`, and in `packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts` it does `credentials.backupCode.replaceAll("-", "")`. If either value is not a string (e.g., object/array/number), `.replaceAll` will be undefined and throw a TypeError, resulting in an unhandled 500 rather than returning `IncorrectBackupCode`/`MissingBackupCodes`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P3: Exhausted backup codes (array of nulls) return IncorrectBackupCode instead of MissingBackupCodes, giving users a misleading message when all codes have been used

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts`, used backup codes are nulled out (`backupCodes[index] = null`) and the encrypted JSON array is kept in `user.backupCodes`. On subsequent login attempts, the code path `if (user.twoFactorEnabled && credentials.backupCode)` only throws `MissingBackupCodes` when `!user.backupCodes` (i.e., the DB field is null/empty), but an exhausted set will be an array of `null`s that still decrypts/JSON-parses successfully. Since `indexOf(input)` on `[null, null, ...]` returns `-1`, the user gets `IncorrectBackupCode` rather than a “no backup codes left” style error. The same pattern exists in `/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts` (checks `!user.backupCodes` then `indexOf(...)`), so the finding is directly supported by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P3: Login page backupCode field may be stripped by zodResolver if not added to formSchema, silently breaking backup-code login; need confirmation schema was updated

adjudication.rationale: In `apps/web/pages/auth/login.tsx`, the form uses `useForm<LoginValues>({ resolver: zodResolver(formSchema) })` and the diff adds a new `backupCode` field (and renders it via the new `BackupCode` component registering `backupCode`). However, this diff does not show any update to the referenced `formSchema` to include `backupCode`. With zodResolver, fields not in the schema can be omitted from the parsed submission payload, potentially breaking backup-code login. This is a valid verification point, but the defect cannot be confirmed from the shown diff alone because `formSchema` is not included here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Note: disable-via-backup-code sets backupCodes to null (deleting all codes) rather than consuming a single code — flagged to confirm this asymmetry with the login flow is intentional

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows an asymmetry: the login flow consumes a single backup code by nulling one entry and re-encrypting the remaining list (packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts), while the 2FA disable endpoint clears backup codes entirely by setting `backupCodes: null` when disabling 2FA (apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts). This isn’t a verifiable defect because disabling 2FA reasonably implies invalidating all backup codes, but it is a concrete behavior difference worth confirming as intentional.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P1: Backup code verification is a non-atomic read-modify-write, allowing a single-use code to be consumed twice via concurrent sign-in requests (next-auth-options.ts ~145-155)
matched_golden_ids: Because backupCodes are decrypted and mutated in memory before being written back, two concurrent login requests using the same backupCode could both pass this check and update, so a single backup code may effectively be accepted more than once if used concurrently, weakening the intended one-time-use semantics.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both describe the same race condition: backup code verification/consumption is a non-atomic read-modify-write, so two concurrent login/sign-in requests can both validate the same backup code before either persists the update, allowing one-time codes to be used more than once.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: Backup code comparison uses indexOf instead of a constant-time comparison like crypto.timingSafeEqual (next-auth-options.ts ~150, disable.ts ~58)

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces backup-code authentication by decrypting an array of codes and checking the user-supplied value via `backupCodes.indexOf(credentials.backupCode.replaceAll("-", ""))` in `packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts` and similarly `backupCodes.indexOf(req.body.backupCode.replaceAll("-", ""))` in `apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts`. This uses ordinary string equality under the hood (not constant-time) and can introduce a timing side-channel for guessing valid backup codes, which is a security defect for an authentication factor.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: disable.ts two-factor endpoint has no per-attempt throttling beyond global rate limiting

adjudication.rationale: In `apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts`, the handler adds a new verification path for `req.body.backupCode` (and still supports TOTP via `req.body.code`), but the diff shows no attempt-level throttling/lockout logic around incorrect `code`/`backupCode` submissions (it just returns 400 with `IncorrectTwoFactorCode` / `IncorrectBackupCode`). The finding’s mention of “beyond global rate limiting” can’t be verified from this diff, but it is correct that this endpoint has no per-attempt throttling visible here, which becomes more relevant with the newly added backup-code disable flow.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: Unhandled JSON.parse on decrypted backup codes with no validation that the result is an array of strings, causing 500s on disable and generic sign-in failures, potentially persisting garbage via write-back, and permanently locking users out of backup-code recovery (disable.ts ~56, next-auth-options.ts ~143)

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...))` for `user.backupCodes` in both the disable endpoint (`apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts`) and NextAuth authorize (`packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts`) with no try/catch and no validation that the parsed value is an array of strings. If the decrypted payload is malformed JSON or not an array (e.g., legacy/corrupted DB value), `JSON.parse` or subsequent `.indexOf(...)` will throw, producing 500s / generic sign-in failures. The diff shows no guard/normalization beyond checking `user.backupCodes` exists, so this is a real robustness defect exposed by the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: req.body.backupCode.replaceAll called without type checking, causing unhandled 500 crash when backupCode is not a string (disable.ts ~58)

adjudication.rationale: In `apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts`, the new backup-code branch runs when `user.twoFactorEnabled && req.body.backupCode` is truthy, then calls `req.body.backupCode.replaceAll("-", "")`. This only checks truthiness, not that `backupCode` is a string. If a client sends a non-string truthy value (e.g., number/object), `replaceAll` will be undefined and throw a `TypeError`, resulting in a 500 response instead of a controlled 4xx error.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: Setup endpoint overwrites user.backupCodes before 2FA is enabled, silently destroying a user's existing valid recovery codes if setup is abandoned (setup.ts ~60-66)

adjudication.rationale: In `apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/setup.ts`, the setup endpoint now generates `backupCodes` and immediately persists them via `prisma.user.update({ data: { backupCodes: symmetricEncrypt(...), twoFactorEnabled: false, twoFactorSecret: ... }})` before 2FA is actually enabled. If a user already had valid backup codes (or triggers setup and abandons before completing enable / seeing the codes), this overwrites the stored `users.backupCodes` with a new set the user may never record, effectively destroying previously valid recovery codes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P3: No UI or endpoint to re-display backup codes; users who close the modal without saving are locked into TOTP-only with codes never recorded (EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx)

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds generation/storage of backup codes during 2FA setup (`/api/auth/two-factor/totp/setup.ts` returns `backupCodes` and stores them encrypted on the user), and the UI only displays them in a one-time `SetupStep.DisplayBackupCodes` state in `EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx`. There is no API route/UI in this diff to fetch or re-display already-generated backup codes later; `setup.ts` is the only place they’re returned, and the disable endpoint even clears them (`backupCodes: null`). So if a user dismisses the modal at the backup-code step without copying/downloading, the codes remain stored but are not retrievable via any shown UI/endpoint, leaving recovery dependent on TOTP. This is a real, diff-grounded product/UX gap rather than a strictly broken behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: setup.ts lacks the encryption key null-check that disable.ts has, though it follows the file's pre-existing pattern

adjudication.rationale: In `apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/setup.ts`, the new code encrypts backup codes via `symmetricEncrypt(JSON.stringify(backupCodes), process.env.CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY)` (and it already encrypts `twoFactorSecret` the same way) without checking that `CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY` is set. By contrast, `disable.ts` now explicitly checks for the env var before decrypting backup codes and errors if missing. The diff shows an inconsistency and a potential missing explicit error-handling path in `setup.ts`, but whether this causes a real runtime defect depends on how `symmetricEncrypt` behaves with an undefined key (not shown in the diff).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Object URL leak in EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx (~line 92-99): createObjectURL result is never revoked on component unmount, leaking a Blob per modal open/setup/close cycle
matched_golden_ids: Object URL for backup codes is not revoked on component unmount, leading to a potential memory leak. This can cause increased memory usage over time, especially if the component is mounted and unmounted frequently.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate issue flags that createObjectURL is used without revoking the resulting Object URL on unmount/close, causing a Blob/object URL memory leak across modal open/close cycles. This is the same underlying issue described in the golden comment (unrevoked Object URL on component unmount leading to memory growth).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Backup-code 'mark used' operation in next-auth-options.ts (~line 140-150) rewrites and re-encrypts the entire JSON array on every backup-code login instead of a targeted update (per-login write amplification)

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts`, when a backup code is used the code decrypts the stored JSON array, sets `backupCodes[index] = null`, then persists it via `prisma.user.update({ data: { backupCodes: symmetricEncrypt(JSON.stringify(backupCodes), ...) } })`. This necessarily rewrites/re-encrypts the entire JSON blob in the `users.backupCodes` TEXT column on each successful backup-code login, matching the finding’s “write amplification” concern. However, given the schema stores all codes in a single TEXT field, a truly “targeted update” isn’t possible without a schema/design change, so this is an architectural/performance concern rather than a correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: setup.ts regenerates/overwrites backup codes on every setup call even if 2FA setup is later abandoned (correctness/security concern)

adjudication.rationale: In `apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/setup.ts`, backup codes are generated on every setup call (`const backupCodes = ...`) and immediately persisted to the user record (`backupCodes: symmetricEncrypt(JSON.stringify(backupCodes), ...)`) alongside resetting `twoFactorEnabled: false`. This means merely initiating setup (even if the user never completes the enable step) rotates/overwrites stored backup codes. While not an immediate functional break (backup codes are only accepted when `twoFactorEnabled` is true), it is a real, diff-grounded edge-case/scope concern because it changes durable credentials before the user has actually enabled/confirmed 2FA.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Null-sentinel JSON array for backup codes in next-auth-options.ts will serialize null entries (correctness/security concern)

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts`, when a backup code is used the code does `backupCodes[index] = null;` and then persists `symmetricEncrypt(JSON.stringify(backupCodes), ...)`, which will store a JSON array containing `null` entries. This is verifiable from the diff. However, based on the shown logic, `indexOf(credentials.backupCode.replaceAll("-", ""))` will still not match `null`, so used codes won’t be reusable; the diff doesn’t show a concrete correctness/security break from the `null` sentinel itself (it’s more of a design/edge-case concern for downstream consumers, e.g., treating “no backup codes” vs “all used”).

adjudication_records.issue_text: backupCode likely stripped by zod schema before reaching NextAuth credentials provider: formSchema not updated in diff, so zodResolver drops backupCode from submit payload, silently breaking backup-code login

adjudication.rationale: In `apps/web/pages/auth/login.tsx`, the form is still created with `useForm<LoginValues>({ resolver: zodResolver(formSchema) })` while `LoginValues` now includes `backupCode` and the UI toggles to a `<BackupCode />` input. The diff does not show any update to `formSchema` to include `backupCode`. With Zod’s default object behavior (unknown keys stripped), a schema that doesn’t declare `backupCode` would drop it from the submitted values, so NextAuth credentials (`credentials.backupCode`) would never receive the backup code, breaking backup-code login.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unvalidated req.body.backupCode type can throw TypeError in totp/disable endpoint, returning unhandled 500 instead of documented 400 ErrorCode.IncorrectBackupCode response

adjudication.rationale: In `apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts`, the backup-code path checks only truthiness (`if (user.twoFactorEnabled && req.body.backupCode)`) and then calls `req.body.backupCode.replaceAll("-", "")`. If `backupCode` is not a string (e.g., object/number), this will throw a `TypeError` at runtime, leading to an unhandled 500 rather than the intended 400 with `ErrorCode.IncorrectBackupCode` (or similar). The diff shows no type validation/normalization before calling `replaceAll`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Setup endpoint response adds backupCodes field but client (EnableTwoFactorModal) calls body.backupCodes.map with no existence check, crashing on stale API/older backend and leaving 2FA in half-configured state

adjudication.rationale: In EnableTwoFactorModal.handleSetup(), after a 200 response it uses `body.backupCodes.map(formatBackupCode)` to build a Blob URL without checking `body.backupCodes` exists (`const textBlob = new Blob([body.backupCodes.map(...).join("\n")], ...)`). The paired setup endpoint in this same diff now returns `{ ..., backupCodes }`, so within this PR’s matched frontend+backend it won’t crash. The concern is about robustness/backward compatibility (frontend assuming a new response field), which is a real diff-grounded issue but not a demonstrable bug given the updated API in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Disable endpoint consumes backup codes differently from login flow (code validated but not burned individually), creating a latent contract asymmetry if an early return is added between validation and final update

adjudication.rationale: In the disable endpoint (`apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts`), when a `backupCode` is provided it is validated and then the handler continues to the final `prisma.user.update` which sets `backupCodes: null` and disables 2FA. So the code path that succeeds does “burn” backup codes by deleting them all, which is a reasonable/intentional difference from the login flow (which burns a single code). The finding’s risk hinges on a hypothetical “early return added between validation and final update,” which is not present in this diff and can’t be verified as an introduced defect here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P1: Backup code single-use enforcement has a race condition — non-atomic read-modify-write (decrypt → indexOf → prisma.user.update of whole array) allows a backup code to be used twice under concurrent login requests; no transaction, conditional UPDATE, or row lock in packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts:148-155

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds backup-code login in `packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts` where it decrypts `user.backupCodes`, checks `indexOf(credentials.backupCode.replaceAll("-", ""))`, then marks the entry `null` and persists the entire array via `prisma.user.update({ data: { backupCodes: symmetricEncrypt(JSON.stringify(backupCodes), ...) } })`. This is a classic non-atomic read-modify-write sequence with no transaction/locking/conditional update, so two concurrent authorize requests using the same backup code can both pass the `indexOf` check before either update commits, allowing the same backup code to be accepted twice.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: Unguarded JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...)) — corrupt stored backupCodes throws an unhandled exception, returning a 500 in the API route and a generic auth failure in authorize, leaving the user with no path to disable or recover 2FA (apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts:56, packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts:139-141)

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new backup-code flows that do `JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(user.backupCodes, ...))` without any guarding/try-catch both in the disable API route (`apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts`, new backupCode branch) and in NextAuth authorize (`packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts`, backupCode branch). If `user.backupCodes` is malformed/corrupted or decrypt returns non-JSON, `JSON.parse` will throw, leading to an unhandled exception path (500 in the API route / thrown auth error), and the diff does not show any local handling to convert this into a user-actionable error.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: ErrorCode.InternalServerError is thrown rather than returned in the disable endpoint, producing a raw 500 HTML page instead of the JSON { error } shape clients expect to parse via response.json() (apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts:47)

adjudication.rationale: In `apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts`, the new backup-code branch does `throw new Error(ErrorCode.InternalServerError)` when `CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY` is missing. That will result in an unhandled exception and a generic 500 response (often HTML) rather than the consistent `res.status(...).json({ error: ... })` shape that clients parse with `response.json()`. This behavior is directly introduced by the added code path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: Unvalidated backupCode body type — req.body.backupCode used directly; a non-string (number, object) makes replaceAll throw, causing an unhandled 500; credentials.backupCode in next-auth-options.ts is similarly not runtime-validated

adjudication.rationale: In `apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts`, the branch `if (user.twoFactorEnabled && req.body.backupCode)` uses `req.body.backupCode.replaceAll("-", "")` without checking it’s a string. If a client sends a truthy non-string (e.g., `{}`), this will throw `TypeError: replaceAll is not a function`, leading to an unhandled 500 in this handler. The same pattern exists in `packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts` where `credentials.backupCode.replaceAll(...)` is called without runtime type validation.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: Backup codes persisted at setup time before 2FA is enabled and never regenerated — abandoned setup leaves stored codes, closing the DisplayBackupCodes step without copying loses the codes permanently, and there is no regenerate path short of disabling and re-enabling 2FA (apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/setup.ts:60-65)

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows backup codes are generated and persisted during the *setup* call even while `twoFactorEnabled` is explicitly set to `false` (`apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/setup.ts` writes `backupCodes: symmetricEncrypt(...)` alongside `twoFactorEnabled: false`). The UI only ever displays the codes from that one setup response, and the “close” action resets local state (`resetState()` clears `password/error/step`, and `backupCodes` aren’t preserved) and calls `onEnable()` without any guard/ack that the user copied/downloaded them (`EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx`, DisplayBackupCodes step). The diff also doesn’t add any endpoint/UI to re-display or regenerate existing stored backup codes after enabling, other than implicitly going through setup again (not shown) or disabling (which nulls `backupCodes` in `totp/disable.ts`). The finding’s “never regenerated” phrasing is somewhat overstated (setup will generate new ones each time it’s called), but the core issue—persisting codes before enable and potential user loss of access to the displayed codes—is grounded in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P3: navigator.clipboard used without availability guard in EnableTwoFactorModal copy handler — undefined in non-secure contexts (plain HTTP, some webviews), so the click throws silently with no feedback or fallback

adjudication.rationale: In EnableTwoFactorModal, the “copy” button handler calls `navigator.clipboard.writeText(...)` directly (added in the diff) with no feature-detection (`navigator.clipboard`), no secure-context check, and no error handling/feedback. In environments where the Clipboard API is unavailable (e.g., non-secure contexts, some embedded/webviews) this can throw at click time and the UI will not show a useful fallback, matching the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P3: Backup code matching is case-sensitive — codes are lowercase hex but compared verbatim, so uppercase input is rejected as incorrect; should normalize with .toLowerCase() on both sides (next-auth-options.ts:145, disable.ts:58)
matched_golden_ids: Backup code validation is case-sensitive due to the use of indexOf(). This causes validation to fail if a user enters uppercase hex characters, as backup codes should be case-insensitive for a better user experience.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags that backup code comparison is case-sensitive and rejects uppercase hex input, and recommends normalizing case (e.g., toLowerCase). This is the same underlying issue as the golden comment about indexOf()-based case-sensitive validation causing uppercase hex to fail.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P3: Object URL never revoked on dialog close/unmount in EnableTwoFactorModal — backupCodesUrl is revoked only when replaced, so blob leaks accumulate per setup attempt

adjudication.rationale: In EnableTwoFactorModal, a Blob URL is created via `URL.createObjectURL(textBlob)` and stored in `backupCodesUrl`. The code only revokes the previous URL when creating a new one (`if (backupCodesUrl) URL.revokeObjectURL(backupCodesUrl);`), but `resetState()` (used on cancel/close) does not revoke or clear `backupCodesUrl`, and there is no effect cleanup on unmount/dialog close. This leaves at least one object URL alive longer than needed (resource leak). The finding’s “accumulate per setup attempt” is somewhat overstated since replacement revokes the previous URL, but the missing revoke on close/unmount is verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Core backup-code authentication logic (decrypt, match, consume, disable-path deletion) has zero unit/integration test coverage and is only exercised indirectly via E2E

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds nontrivial backup-code auth logic in multiple server paths—generation/encryption in `pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/setup.ts`, backup-code verification (decrypt + match) and disable-path handling in `pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts`, and backup-code login + consumption/re-encryption in `packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts`. The only test change is in `apps/web/playwright/login.2fa.e2e.ts`, which exercises UI actions (download/copy/close) and does not directly assert the decrypt/match/consume behaviors. No unit/integration tests for these new codepaths are added in the diff, so the finding is a specific, diff-grounded coverage gap rather than a functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: MissingBackupCodes branch for users with null user.backupCodes (pre-existing 2FA users) is untested

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces explicit handling for pre-existing 2FA users with no stored backup codes: in the disable API it returns `ErrorCode.MissingBackupCodes` when `user.twoFactorEnabled && req.body.backupCode` but `!user.backupCodes` (apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts), and in NextAuth authorize it throws `MissingBackupCodes` when `credentials.backupCode` is provided but `user.backupCodes` is null (packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts). The added Playwright test only covers showing/downloading/copying codes after enabling 2FA, and even includes a TODO to add more backup code tests; there is no test exercising the `MissingBackupCodes` branch for users who already had 2FA enabled before this migration (backupCodes null).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Malformed/stale backupCodes JSON causing JSON.parse to throw an unhandled 500 is untested

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `JSON.parse(...)` on decrypted `user.backupCodes` in two places without guarding against malformed/corrupted data: `apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts` (`const backupCodes = JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...))`) and `packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts` (same pattern). If the stored `backupCodes` string is stale/corrupted or decrypts to non-JSON, `JSON.parse` will throw and result in an unhandled server error (500). The PR adds only UI/e2e coverage for displaying/downloading/copying codes and does not add tests for this failure mode.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Single-use property of backup codes (consumed code set to null cannot authenticate again) is untested

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds single-use consumption for backup codes in `packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts`: when `credentials.backupCode` is used, the matched entry is nulled (`backupCodes[index] = null`) and the updated list is re-encrypted and persisted via `prisma.user.update(...)`. However, the added Playwright test (`apps/web/playwright/login.2fa.e2e.ts`) only verifies download/copy/close UI for displayed codes and even includes a TODO about adding more backup code tests; it does not attempt a backup-code login twice to ensure the consumed (nulled) code cannot authenticate again. So the finding is a specific, diff-grounded missing-test gap for newly added nontrivial logic, not a runtime defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: E2E test contains a self-admitted false-positive assertion (FIXME) using isChecked() instead of data-state="checked" check

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly adds a FIXME in `apps/web/playwright/login.2fa.e2e.ts` noting that `expect(page.locator('[data-testid=two-factor-switch]').isChecked()).toBeTruthy();` “passes even when switch is not checked” and suggests using the `data-state="checked"` assertion used later. This indicates a known unreliable/false-positive test assertion introduced/retained in the updated E2E test, which is a concrete review issue but not a product/runtime defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Advertised backup-code flows (login with backup code, disable 2FA with backup code) explicitly not tested (TODO)

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new backup-code functionality for both login and 2FA disable (e.g., `credentials.backupCode` handling in `packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts` and `backupCode` handling in `apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts`), but the Playwright coverage explicitly notes these flows are not tested: `apps/web/playwright/login.2fa.e2e.ts` contains `// TODO: add more backup code tests, e.g. login + disabling 2fa with backup`. The existing added tests only cover showing/copying/downloading backup codes after enabling, not using them to login or disable 2FA.

adjudication_records.issue_text: E2E download and copy checks are stub-level: file content and clipboard content not verified

adjudication.rationale: In `apps/web/playwright/login.2fa.e2e.ts`, the newly added backup-code UI checks only assert `download.suggestedFilename()` and that a success toast appears after clicking copy, while explicitly leaving `// TODO: check file content` and `// TODO: check clipboard content`. That means the E2E test does not verify the downloaded file contains the expected backup codes nor that the clipboard was populated correctly, making the added coverage fairly stub-level for this new functionality.

adjudication_records.issue_text: New server-side branches in disable.ts untested: wrong password ordering, backupCode without 2FA, and backupCodes wiped on successful disable

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new, nontrivial server-side branch in `apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts` for `user.twoFactorEnabled && req.body.backupCode` (decrypting/statically checking backup codes and returning new errors), and also changes successful disable to always set `backupCodes: null` in the Prisma update. No tests in this PR cover disabling 2FA via backup code (the existing Playwright additions only cover displaying/downloading/copying backup codes during enable, and even include a TODO about more backup code tests). The finding’s subpoint about “wrong password ordering” isn’t clearly verifiable from the shown diff, but the core concern (new branches/behaviors in disable.ts lacking coverage) is diff-grounded and actionable.

adjudication_records.issue_text: DisableTwoFactorModal 'lost access' toggle and new error branches lack component or E2E coverage

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds nontrivial new UI and branching logic in `DisableTwoFactorModal`: a `twoFactorLostAccess` toggle that switches between `<TwoFactor .../>` and the new `<BackupCode .../>` component, plus new error handling branches for `IncorrectBackupCode` and `MissingBackupCodes` (and the API now posts `backupCode`). However, the only test changes shown are in `apps/web/playwright/login.2fa.e2e.ts`, which explicitly contains a `TODO` for backup code tests and does not cover disabling 2FA or the modal toggle/error paths. No component/unit/E2E coverage is added for these new DisableTwoFactorModal behaviors.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Login page three-state navigation (password → TOTP → backup code) untested, including field clearing on back navigation

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new login UI/state transitions for a 3-state flow: normal login → TOTP (`twoFactorRequired`) → backup code (`twoFactorLostAccess`) with field-reset logic in `TwoFactorFooter` (clearing `totpCode`/`backupCode` and `errorMessage`) and a new `lost_access` button in `apps/web/pages/auth/login.tsx`. However, the only touched Playwright test (`apps/web/playwright/login.2fa.e2e.ts`) adds coverage for displaying/copying/downloading backup codes during *enable* flow, and even includes a TODO for adding more backup code tests, but it does not exercise the login page’s new TOTP↔backup navigation or verify field clearing on back navigation. This is a concrete missing test for newly added nontrivial UI logic, not a directly verifiable functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: IncorrectBackupCode/MissingBackupCodes error handling replacing SecondFactorRequired chain unverified: bad backup code should keep user on backup screen with retry/back

adjudication.rationale: The diff already keeps the user on the current 2FA mode when IncorrectBackupCode/MissingBackupCodes occurs: in `login.tsx` the handler only sets `errorMessage` for these errors and does not toggle `twoFactorLostAccess` or `twoFactorRequired`, so if the user is on the backup-code screen (`twoFactorLostAccess === true`) they remain there and can retry or use the existing back buttons. Similarly, `DisableTwoFactorModal.tsx` only sets an error message for `IncorrectBackupCode`/`MissingBackupCodes` and does not change `twoFactorLostAccess`, so the modal stays on the backup-code input when that mode is active. The claim that error handling causes leaving the backup screen is not supported by the shown changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: PasswordField tabIndex={-1} changes keyboard accessibility app-wide with no test or explicit callout

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes the password-visibility toggle button inside `PasswordField` to `tabIndex={-1}` (`packages/ui/components/form/inputs/Input.tsx`), which removes it from the keyboard tab order. That is an app-wide accessibility regression for keyboard-only users (they can no longer focus/activate the toggle via Tab), and the diff does not add any tests or documentation/callout around this behavioral change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Code matching edge cases untested: case/whitespace not normalized (uppercase input hard-fails), inconsistent length validation between BackupCode.tsx (10/11) and disable endpoint

adjudication.rationale: Backup codes are generated as lowercase hex (setup.ts: `crypto.randomBytes(5).toString("hex")`) and matching is done via `indexOf(req.body.backupCode.replaceAll("-", ""))` (disable.ts) / `credentials.backupCode.replaceAll("-", "")` (next-auth-options) with no `trim()`/`toLowerCase()`. This means user-entered uppercase or whitespace-padded codes will not match, which is a real edge-case robustness issue. However, the stated “inconsistent length validation” isn’t clearly substantiated: the UI enforces 10/11 chars and the server comparison effectively requires the 10-char post-dash-removal value to match, so there’s no demonstrable mismatch in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Closing backup-codes dialog via native close skips resetState()/onEnable(), leaving stale state; modal reopening and object-URL revoke path untested

adjudication.rationale: In EnableTwoFactorModal, resetState() (and onEnable()) are only invoked via explicit button handlers (Cancel and the "backup-codes-close" button). The Dialog itself is controlled by `open`/`onOpenChange`, but there is no handler/effect that resets state when the user closes the dialog via the native dialog close mechanisms (e.g., DialogContent "X" or outside click triggering `onOpenChange(false)`). That can leave `step` stuck on `DisplayBackupCodes` and `backupCodesUrl` retained across reopen, and the object URL is only revoked when a new one is created (`if (backupCodesUrl) URL.revokeObjectURL(backupCodesUrl);`), not on close/unmount.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Duplicated backup-code verification logic in next-auth-options.ts:131-153 and disable.ts:47-63 should be extracted into a shared helper like verifyBackupCode(user, code)

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds backup-code verification in two places with very similar steps (check CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY, ensure user.backupCodes exists, symmetricDecrypt + JSON.parse, normalize by removing dashes, indexOf match, and error handling): in `packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts` (new `if (user.twoFactorEnabled && credentials.backupCode) { ... }`) and in `apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts` (new `if (user.twoFactorEnabled && req.body.backupCode) { ... }`). This is real duplication introduced by the change and could be extracted to a shared helper to reduce divergence risk, but it is not itself a functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Backup codes are never consumed/invalidated when disabling 2FA via backup code; a failed disable after a successful match leaves the verified code reusable indefinitely

adjudication.rationale: In the disable endpoint (`apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts`), when `user.twoFactorEnabled && req.body.backupCode` matches a stored backup code, the request proceeds to the final `prisma.user.update` which explicitly sets `backupCodes: null` while disabling 2FA (`twoFactorEnabled: false`, `twoFactorSecret: null`). So backup codes are invalidated upon a successful disable via backup code. The finding’s claim that backup codes are “never consumed/invalidated” is contradicted by this update. Any “failed disable after successful match” scenario would require an unshown/exceptional failure after verification (e.g., DB error), which the diff does not establish as a concrete bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: backupCodesUrl blob URL created via URL.createObjectURL in EnableTwoFactorModal is never revoked on unmount or flow completion, leaking blob URLs containing plaintext backup codes

adjudication.rationale: In EnableTwoFactorModal, a blob URL containing plaintext backup codes is created via `URL.createObjectURL(textBlob)` and stored in state (`backupCodesUrl`). The only revocation is conditional when creating a *new* URL (`if (backupCodesUrl) URL.revokeObjectURL(backupCodesUrl);`). However, `resetState()` (used on cancel/close flow completion) does not revoke or clear `backupCodesUrl`, and there is no `useEffect` cleanup to revoke on unmount. This leaves the blob URL alive after the modal flow ends/unmounts, leaking resources and keeping a URL to sensitive plaintext in memory longer than necessary.

adjudication_records.issue_text: resetState() in EnableTwoFactorModal clears password/error/step but not backupCodes/backupCodesUrl, leaving sensitive material lingering in component state

adjudication.rationale: In `EnableTwoFactorModal`, `resetState()` only calls `setPassword("")`, `setErrorMessage(null)`, and `setStep(SetupStep.ConfirmPassword)` but does not clear `backupCodes` (`useState([])`) nor `backupCodesUrl` (`useState("")`). Since backup codes are set on successful `/totp/setup` (`setBackupCodes(body.backupCodes)`) and an object URL is created/stored (`setBackupCodesUrl(URL.createObjectURL(textBlob))`), invoking `resetState()` on cancel/close leaves sensitive backup codes and a live download URL lingering in component state (and the object URL is not revoked unless a new one is created).

adjudication_records.issue_text: setup.ts calls symmetricEncrypt with process.env.CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY without checking the key exists, unlike sibling endpoints; unset key could cause an unhandled 500 mid-setup or encryption with undefined key producing garbage

adjudication.rationale: In `apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/setup.ts`, the PR adds `backupCodes: symmetricEncrypt(JSON.stringify(backupCodes), process.env.CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY)` (and the existing `twoFactorSecret: symmetricEncrypt(secret, process.env.CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY)`) without any guard that `CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY` is set. In contrast, the new backup-code flows in `totp/disable.ts` and `next-auth-options.ts` explicitly check for the env var and error out. If the key is unset, setup can throw or produce invalid encrypted data, resulting in a server error mid-setup and/or corrupted stored values.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unchecked JSON.parse on decrypted stored backup codes will throw on malformed/legacy values, causing an unhandled 500 in disable.ts or opaque auth failure in next-auth; should be wrapped in try/catch surfacing MissingBackupCodes/InternalServerError

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces backup code handling that does `JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...))` without any try/catch in both `apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts` and `packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts`. If `user.backupCodes` contains malformed JSON (e.g., legacy/non-JSON, corrupted ciphertext, wrong key, partial writes), `JSON.parse` will throw and (a) in the API route cause an unhandled exception/500, and (b) in next-auth `authorize` cause a thrown error that may surface as an opaque auth failure. The only guard added is `if (!user.backupCodes)`; it does not prevent parse/decrypt exceptions.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Dialog onOpenChange (backdrop/ESC close) in EnableTwoFactorModal doesn't call resetState(), so reopening after closing at DisplayBackupCodes re-displays old backup codes instead of starting at ConfirmPassword

adjudication.rationale: In EnableTwoFactorModal, internal state (step, password, errorMessage, backupCodes/backupCodesUrl) is only reset via the explicit Cancel button handler and the DisplayBackupCodes “close” button. The Dialog is wired as `<Dialog open={open} onOpenChange={onOpenChange}>` without wrapping `onOpenChange` to call `resetState()` when the dialog closes via ESC/backdrop. If the component remains mounted (common for controlled dialogs), closing and reopening can preserve `step === DisplayBackupCodes` and the prior `backupCodes`, re-displaying them instead of restarting at ConfirmPassword.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Backup-code comparison uses non-constant-time indexOf string equality; should use crypto.timingSafeEqual for security-sensitive credential verification

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces backup code verification using `Array.indexOf` on decrypted codes (e.g. `backupCodes.indexOf(req.body.backupCode.replaceAll("-", ""))` in `apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts` and similarly in `packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts`). This relies on normal string equality and short-circuits on first match/non-match, which is not constant-time and can leak information via timing in a credential-checking path. For security-sensitive secret verification, a constant-time comparison (e.g., `crypto.timingSafeEqual` with fixed-length buffers and a constant-time scan) is the safer approach.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Component in BackupCode.tsx is named TwoFactor, mismatching the file and import name BackupCode, a maintenance trap conflating it with the real TwoFactor component
matched_golden_ids: The exported function TwoFactor handles backup codes and is in BackupCode.tsx. Inconsistent naming.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both comments flag the same underlying issue: the component/export in BackupCode.tsx is named TwoFactor, which is inconsistent with the file/import name BackupCode and can cause confusion/maintenance problems.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Backup-code XXXXX-XXXXX format logic is implicitly duplicated across formatBackupCode, BackupCode placeholder, and two dash-strip call sites with no shared constant

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows the backup-code format/normalization logic repeated in multiple places: `formatBackupCode` in `EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx` (slicing 0-5 and 5-10 with a dash), the UI placeholder in `BackupCode.tsx` (`"XXXXX-XXXXX"`), and at least two server-side normalization call sites stripping dashes via `.replaceAll("-", "")` (in `pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts` and `packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts`). This is a maintainability/consistency risk (format rules could drift) but not a directly verifiable functional defect in the diff as-is.

adjudication_records.issue_text: New i18n keys (backup_code, lost_access, etc.) added only to the en locale; other locales will render raw keys or fall back

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new translation keys only in `apps/web/public/static/locales/en/common.json` (e.g. `backup_code`, `lost_access`, `missing_backup_codes`, etc.) and does not show corresponding additions in other locale JSON files. That’s a concrete i18n coverage gap introduced by this change, though whether it renders raw keys vs. fallback behavior isn’t directly verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [P1, confidence 75] Backup code consumption is not atomic — read-modify-write race allows a single-use backup code to be consumed twice by concurrent login requests (next-auth-options.ts)

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts`, backup code verification/consumption is implemented as a non-atomic read-modify-write: decrypt `user.backupCodes`, locate the matching entry, then set `backupCodes[index] = null` and `prisma.user.update({ data: { backupCodes: symmetricEncrypt(...) } })`. With two concurrent login requests using the same backup code, both can read the same pre-update value, both pass `index !== -1`, and both successfully update (writing essentially the same "consumed" state). There is no transaction/conditional update to ensure only one request can consume the code, so a single-use code can be accepted twice under race.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [P1, confidence 75] Backup codes are displayed only once; closing the dialog at DisplayBackupCodes step (ESC/backdrop) stores codes on the user row without ever showing them, permanently locking the user out with no recovery path; stale state also persists on reopen

adjudication.rationale: In EnableTwoFactorModal, reaching SetupStep.DisplayBackupCodes is the only place where the flow calls `onEnable()` and `resetState()` (via the “close” button handler). However the Dialog can also be closed via `onOpenChange` (ESC/backdrop), and this component does not reset state or call `onEnable()` when `open` becomes false. As a result, closing the modal at the DisplayBackupCodes step via ESC/backdrop can leave the parent UI unaware that 2FA was enabled (since `onEnable()` isn’t called) and can leave sensitive `backupCodes`/`backupCodesUrl` state persisted across reopen because `resetState()` is not triggered on modal close. This is directly observable from the diff: state is only reset in the cancel button handler (not shown in DisplayBackupCodes) and in the backup-codes-close button; there is no effect/handler tied to `onOpenChange` to cleanup.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [P2, confidence 75] setup.ts overwrites user.backupCodes at the password-confirm step, so abandoning enable flow mid-way wipes previous codes and replaces them with codes the user never saw; also silently sets twoFactorEnabled: false

adjudication.rationale: In `apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/setup.ts`, the setup endpoint now generates `backupCodes` and immediately persists them (and also writes `twoFactorEnabled: false` and a new `twoFactorSecret`) via `prisma.user.update(...)` before the user has completed enabling 2FA. In the UI (`EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx`), `handleSetup` calls this setup endpoint at the password-confirm step and stores `body.backupCodes` in state, but the modal does not display backup codes until *after* successful enable (`handleEnable` sets `step` to `DisplayBackupCodes`). If the user cancels/abandons the flow after setup (e.g., during QR-code step), `resetState()` clears local state and the user may never see the newly generated codes, while the server-side `backupCodes` have already been overwritten. This is a verifiable data-loss/behavior bug introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [P2, confidence 50] Malformed or undecryptable backupCodes data causes symmetricDecrypt/JSON.parse to throw an unhandled 500 instead of the intended graceful MissingBackupCodes error path (disable.ts and next-auth-options.ts)

adjudication.rationale: In both `apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts` and `packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts`, the code assumes `user.backupCodes` is decryptable JSON: `JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...))`. Only the `null/undefined` case is handled (`MissingBackupCodes`), but if the stored value is corrupted, encrypted with a different key, or not valid JSON, `symmetricDecrypt` and/or `JSON.parse` will throw. There is no surrounding `try/catch`, so the request/authorize flow will error out (500 / unhandled error) rather than returning the intended structured error path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: Backup code matching is case/format sensitive; valid codes silently rejected due to no toLowerCase/trim in next-auth-options.ts:146 and disable.ts:57 (confidence 75)

adjudication.rationale: Backup codes are generated as lowercase hex (`crypto.randomBytes(5).toString("hex")` in `setup.ts`), but both verification paths compare with a raw `indexOf()` after only removing dashes (`credentials.backupCode.replaceAll("-", "")` in `next-auth-options.ts` and `req.body.backupCode.replaceAll("-", "")` in `disable.ts`). There is no `trim()` or case normalization, so inputs like uppercase codes (or codes with leading/trailing spaces) that represent the same code can be rejected as `IncorrectBackupCode`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: Single-use backup code guarantee is not atomic; concurrent use can match and succeed twice via read-modify-write in next-auth-options.ts ~143-155 (confidence 75)

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts`, backup code validation performs a decrypt + `indexOf` match, then marks the matched entry as `null` and writes the whole array back via a separate `prisma.user.update(...)`. This is a classic read-modify-write sequence without any transactional/conditional update, so two concurrent authorize calls using the same backup code can both read the old `backupCodes`, both find the code, and both succeed before either update is persisted—violating the “single-use” guarantee.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: Known-broken e2e assertion in login.2fa.e2e.ts:50-51 (FIXME: passes even when switch is not checked) acts as silent-pass gate for the enable flow (confidence 100)

adjudication.rationale: In `apps/web/playwright/login.2fa.e2e.ts`, the assertion `await expect(page.locator(...).isChecked()).toBeTruthy();` is effectively a silent-pass because `locator.isChecked()` returns a `Promise<boolean>` and it is not awaited before being passed to `expect`. A Promise object is always truthy, so this can pass even when the switch is not checked—matching the added `FIXME` comment in the diff. This weakens the enable-2FA flow gate in the test.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: EnableTwoFactorModal dialog dismissal at DisplayBackupCodes step bypasses both resetState and onEnable, leaving stale state and no way back; blob URL also never revoked on unmount (confidence 50)

adjudication.rationale: In EnableTwoFactorModal, the DisplayBackupCodes step hides the Cancel button and only resets state/calls onEnable via the explicit “close” button handler. If the Dialog is dismissed via onOpenChange (e.g., overlay click / ESC / built-in close control), this component does not call resetState() or onEnable(), so internal state (step, password, backupCodes, backupCodesUrl) can remain stale when reopened. Separately, backupCodesUrl is created with URL.createObjectURL(...) and only revoked when creating a new one; there is no unmount/cleanup revoke, so the blob URL can leak.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P3: Disable endpoint unvalidated backupCode type causes unhandled TypeError/500 instead of 400 in disable.ts:57 (confidence 75)

adjudication.rationale: In `apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts`, the new backup-code branch checks `if (user.twoFactorEnabled && req.body.backupCode)` and then immediately calls `req.body.backupCode.replaceAll("-", "")`. There is no runtime validation that `req.body.backupCode` is a string. If a client sends a truthy non-string (e.g., `{}` or `123`) in JSON, `replaceAll` will throw a `TypeError`, likely resulting in an unhandled 500 instead of a controlled 400 error response.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P3: DisableTwoFactorModal in backup-code mode: empty backupCode submission falls into TOTP branch server-side, surfacing wrong '2fa required' error (confidence 50)

adjudication.rationale: In the disable API, the backup-code path is only taken when `user.twoFactorEnabled && req.body.backupCode` is truthy (apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts). If the UI is in backup-code mode but submits an empty string (`backupCode: ""`), that condition is false and the request falls into the TOTP branch (`else if (user.twoFactorEnabled)`), which returns `SecondFactorRequired` when `code` is missing. The DisableTwoFactorModal always passes `backupCode` to `TwoFactorAuthAPI.disable(password, totpCode, backupCode)` and does not add react-hook-form validation rules for `backupCode` (it relies on the input's `required` attribute), so this mismatched server-side error is a plausible, diff-grounded behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P3: setup.ts:60-67 persists backup codes at setup step before confirmation, leaving stale encrypted codes at rest for abandoned setups (confidence 50)

adjudication.rationale: In `apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/setup.ts`, the setup endpoint now generates `backupCodes` and immediately persists them to `user.backupCodes` (encrypted) while also keeping `twoFactorEnabled: false`. If the user abandons the flow before completing enable, those encrypted backup codes remain stored indefinitely (there’s no cleanup path when 2FA isn’t enabled). This is a real lifecycle/data-hygiene concern introduced by the diff, but it’s not clearly a functional/security defect because backup codes are only accepted when `user.twoFactorEnabled` is true (see disable/login checks).
